objective: Establish whether a matched solver-constrained versus unconstrained Avocado CIT comparison is locally executable with a held-out configuration model and predeclared invalid-configuration endpoints.

decision.basis: Both generator arms are locally runnable from a public version pin, but the source-matched QEMU configuration oracle, its pinned validation corpus, and a held-out configuration model are not locally available. The available Avocado example files are demonstrations, not the source's industrial QEMU model, and were not substituted as a scientific benchmark.

sources_and_data.title: Towards an Automated Unified Framework to Run Applications for Combinatorial Interaction Testing
observations: The SUT is QEMU block-layer configuration checking with five parameters and 200 full configurations (5^2 × 2^3).
A configuration is valid only if all 192 validation scripts pass; otherwise it is invalid.

The reported endpoints are generated/ executed suite size, total execution time, and detected invalid configurations across t-way strengths; no constrained-versus-unconstrained comparison is reported.
The paper identifies qemu-iotests as the validation-script source but does not pin a repository commit or release in the inspected version.

sources_and_data.title: Avocado: Open-Source Flexible Constrained Interaction Testing for Practical Application
observations: The follow-up implements constrained CIT in Avocado using forbidden tuples derived from CNF constraints and a randomized covering-suite search.

The follow-up defines a valid generated test case as one containing no forbidden tuple; it does not report the frozen matched detection/cost comparison against unconstrained generation on the original QEMU oracle.
The plugin's setup pins the plugin to the same Avocado version.
Solver.py is local Python code using itertools; no external SMT solver is required by this plugin implementation.

sources_and_data.use: generator feasibility smoke only; not treated as the QEMU industrial model or held-out scientific data

frozen_question_and_endpoints.question: On constrained virtual-machine configuration spaces, does solver-backed constraint handling reduce invalid or redundant test executions while preserving or improving detection of invalid configurations relative to unconstrained t-way generation?
arms: constrained: Avocado 100.0 CIT varianter with the frozen CNF constraints
unconstrained: the same Avocado 100.0 CIT generator and t-way strength with an empty constraint set

primary_metrics.invalid_configuration_detection_recall: detected invalid configurations / all invalid configurations in the frozen QEMU validation universe; invalid means at least one of the 192 pinned validation scripts fails
primary_metrics.executed_test_count: number of generated configuration variants sent to the runner, with the same t-way strength and test-runner accounting in both arms
primary_metrics.wall_clock_cost: generation plus execution plus oracle-validation wall time under the same machine and run protocol

frozen_question_and_endpoints.falsification_gate: No reduction in invalid or redundant executions at non-inferior detection recall, or a benefit that disappears on a held-out configuration model, falsifies practical value.

predeclared_protocol: Pin Avocado/plugin at 100.0 and retain the original source version and follow-up version as provenance, not as executable outcomes.
Use identical parameter domains, t-way strength, runner, oracle, seed policy, and cost accounting in both arms.
Freeze a public source-matched training model and a distinct held-out configuration model before generation; do not infer invalidity from the generator's constraint file alone.
Report recall, executed count, invalid-test rate, and wall-clock cost with exact denominators; preserve zero and missing outcomes.
local_commands_and_checks: Ran constrained and empty-constraint generator smoke paths at t=2 on the two public example .cit files; no QEMU execution or endpoint result was claimed.
method.held_out_requirement: A second, source-authenticated configuration model with its own pinned domains/constraints and independently runnable oracle is required; the two example .cit files are not accepted as that model because they are demonstration inputs and do not contain the QEMU validation corpus.

generator_smoke.interpretation: Both arms execute locally, but this smoke does not measure invalid-configuration detection recall, invalid-test rate under the QEMU oracle, or a valid held-out comparison. The zero invalid rows in the smoke is not a scientific null result.

blockers: qemu-img and qemu are absent from the local environment.
The 192 qemu-iotests validation scripts and their exact source revision are absent locally and are not pinned by the inspected 1903.05387v1 source.
The industrial QEMU parameter/constraint model needed to reproduce the constrained arm is not released as a version-pinned .cit artifact in the inspected public Avocado 100.0 source tree.
No independently authenticated held-out configuration model plus executable oracle is available locally.
Therefore invalid-test rate and detection recall cannot be computed without inventing an oracle or substituting a synthetic benchmark.
observed_result_or_blocker.negative_or_null_preserved: No efficacy result, recall estimate, invalid-test-rate estimate, or constrained-versus-unconstrained scientific comparison was observed. This is a bounded feasibility no-go, not evidence that constrained Avocado is ineffective.

uncertainty: The public follow-up establishes implementation partial progress, but not the frozen matched outcome.
Avocado's randomized generator makes small generator-only smoke counts seed-dependent; those counts are not compared as scientific effects.
A future QEMU/qemu-iotests checkout could make the experiment feasible if the exact model, constraints, oracle, held-out model, and compatible runtime are pinned together.
The Paper 4 planning information-gain estimate (0.72) was not treated as observed scientific value.
next_falsifiable_action: Acquire or construct an authorized, version-pinned QEMU model and validation bundle: pin the qemu-iotests commit, qemu-img/QEMU build, five parameter domains, industrial constraints, and a distinct held-out configuration model. Then preregister equal-seed constrained/empty-constraint arms at fixed t, run the same 192-script oracle, and compute recall, executed count, invalid-test rate, and wall-clock cost. Stop without a comparison if any artifact or held-out oracle remains missing.
